about: Kirk C. Stange is the President and Founding Partner of Stange Law Firm, PC , a multi-state law firm focused exclusively on divorce, child custody, and other domestic relations matters. He founded the firm in 2007 and has helped guide its growth from a single-office practice into a substantial family law firm serving clients from offices across numerous states. The firm’s mission is reflected in its tagline: “Here to Help You Rebuild Your Life™.”

Throughout his legal career, Kirk has represented clients in complex and emotionally sensitive family law matters involving divorce, child custody and parenting time, property and asset division, child support, spousal maintenance, paternity, prenuptial agreements, and related domestic relations issues. He has substantial courtroom experience involving contested hearings, trials, and appellate matters.

Kirk is trained as a mediator, collaborative law attorney, and guardian ad litem. This training enables him to evaluate domestic relations matters from multiple perspectives, including litigation, negotiated resolution, collaborative practice, and the interests of children affected by family court proceedings.

As Stange Law Firm has grown, Kirk’s responsibilities have expanded beyond direct courtroom advocacy. Today, he devotes much of his time to firm leadership, strategic growth, attorney development, legal education, marketing initiatives, and oversight of the firm’s multi-state domestic relations practice. He remains actively engaged in family law developments and in helping the firm’s attorneys provide effective representation to clients facing difficult family transitions.

Kirk’s personal availability for new representations is limited and determined on a case-by-case basis, with a particular focus on select family law matters in the St. Louis metropolitan area. Prospective clients who contact Stange Law Firm can be connected with an attorney whose experience and location are suited to the particular needs of their case.

Kirk is deeply involved in legal education and professional development. He has presented continuing legal education programs for organizations including The Missouri Bar, the National Business Institute, and other legal education providers. His presentations have addressed family law, trial practice, evidence, legal technology, social media, law practice management, and related topics.

In 2014, Kirk presented at the Eighth Circuit Judicial Conference in Omaha, Nebraska, regarding the use of social media evidence by attorneys and judges. In 2017, The Missouri Bar recognized Kirk in its Best of CLE Spotlight for his substantial contributions to continuing legal education, including his repeated participation in MoBarCLE’s Annual Law Update and advanced family law seminars. He has also served as a mentor through The Missouri Bar Mentoring Program.

Kirk has contributed to legal education in an academic setting as well. He has served as an adjunct professor and trial instructor at Emory University School of Law in the Kessler-Eidson Program for Trial Techniques. He is also a member of the Law Society at the University of Missouri School of Law.

Kirk serves as President of the Missouri Collaborative Institute , an organization dedicated to promoting collaborative practice as an alternative method of resolving divorce and family law disputes. His professional background in litigation, mediation, collaborative law, and child advocacy gives him a broad perspective on the different approaches families may use to address domestic relations matters.

Kirk earned his Bachelor of Arts in History from Fontbonne University and his Juris Doctor from the University of Missouri School of Law. While attending law school, he was selected for membership in the Order of the Barristers, a national honor recognizing excellence in courtroom advocacy. He was also a finalist in the school’s fall moot court competition and participated on its regional moot court team.

On the July 2000 Missouri Bar Examination, Kirk scored in the top ten percent of all examinees. He later completed advanced trial training through the American Bar Association Family Law Trial Advocacy Institute.
Kirk is licensed to practice law in Missouri, Illinois, Kansas, and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri.

Kirk is a published legal author whose work has addressed family law, prenuptial agreements, military divorce, protection orders, child abuse issues in domestic cases, alternative dispute resolution, and law practice management.

In 2014, he authored the full-length book Prenuptial Agreements Line by Line , published by Thomson Reuters/Aspatore Publishing. He also authored the introductory chapter of a 2012 Thomson Reuters/Aspatore book concerning military family law and a chapter in a 2015 Aspatore publication addressing Illinois family law and alternative dispute resolution.

Kirk has also co-authored multiple chapters and updates in Missouri Family Law , published by The Missouri Bar. His contributions include materials addressing adult protection orders, child protection orders, child abuse issues in domestic cases, and the rights of unmarried parents.

Kirk publishes family law analysis through JD Supra and is a member of the Entrepreneur Leadership Network , where he writes about leadership, law firm management, professional development, marketing, and business growth.

Kirk is frequently asked to provide commentary concerning divorce, child custody, prenuptial agreements, law firm leadership, and developments in family law. His media appearances, interviews, and features include:
